heuristics.name: classic-gloss
heuristics.description: Picked the option that is most recognisably the plain-English gloss of a common ISEE Upper headword (e.g. outlaw=prohibit, diligent=industrious). Weak prior, since every option is designed to be such a gloss.

heuristics.name: antonym-pair
heuristics.description: When two options are opposites, assumed the key is one of the pair (antonym planted as distractor) and chose the more typical gloss.

heuristics.name: polysemy
heuristics.description: Options span two senses of one likely headword (e.g. curb: pavement/gutter vs restrain); picked the tested secondary sense.

heuristics.name: near-miss-cluster
heuristics.description: Two options are near-synonyms; assumed one is key and the other a near-miss, picked the more headword-like one.

heuristics.name: repeated-distractor
heuristics.description: A filler word (hollow) recurs across items as a distractor; rejected it and chose the strongest remaining gloss.

notes: Options-only synonym items give little real signal; every option is a plausible gloss. Most signal picks rest on a weak familiarity prior. No reject could be certain without the headword, so reject_certain is false throughout. Letter distribution was not used.
